explanation: The almighty Creator who, according to Genesis, created the heavens, the earth, and all life.
The term used to describe God's act of bringing the universe and everything in it into existence.
The upper part of the universe, including the atmosphere and outer space, created by God in Genesis.
The planet we live on, which was created by God as a place for life and human existence.
All living organisms, including plants, animals, and humans, which God created during the six days of creation.
A period of time used in Genesis to describe the order and duration of God's creative acts.
The first element God created, separating day from night and making sight and growth possible.
A fundamental building block for all life, separated by God into two areas – the sea and the waters above.
Dry ground, separated from the water by God, providing a place for plants, animals, and humans to live.
Living organisms that produce oxygen and nourishment, created by God to provide food and sustenance for animals and humans.
Aquatic animals that God created to populate the seas and serve as a food source for other creatures.
Flying animals that God created to fill the sky and serve as a food source for other creatures.
Living organisms that move and have senses, created by God to populate the earth and serve as food sources and helpers for humans.
The highest form of life, created by God in his own image, with responsibility to rule over and care for the earth and all its creatures.
Likeness and representation of God, in which humanity was created, giving humans a unique position among all other creatures.
